name: Paleoconservatism
summary: Paleoconservatism is an American conservatism that stresses tradition, moral order, Christian ethics, national identity and localism. It favours immigration restriction, protectionism and non-intervention abroad, and opposes neoconservatism, the managerial state and multiculturalism.
scope: The American movement named by Paul Gottfried in the 1980s, drawn from Russell Kirk, Pat Buchanan and the Chronicles and American Conservative circles; most economic and technology answers are inferred. It excludes European traditionalism and the paleolibertarian fusion with the Old Right.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from opposition to federal welfare programs and centralised power; not a defining issue.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economic nationalists and market-minded conservatives within the movement split on wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement unites free-market Old Right heirs with economic nationalists who distrust unfettered markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Kirk ties property to freedom and warns against involuntary collectivism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the property-and-freedom principle; no stated tax program.

unions-good.rationale: Adherents are split; protectionists value industrial workers while Old Right heirs dislike unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Kirk's seventh principle links private property to freedom and stability.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Hostility to multinationals sits beside general opposition to federal regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Paleoconservatives argued welfare damaged local communities and was imposed from above.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred from rejection of collectivism and preference for voluntary community.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the principle of restraints on state power.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on an enduring moral order and traditional morality.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from hostility to multiculturalism and political correctness programs.

strong-leader.rationale: Kirk calls for checks and limits on power; paleoconservatives champion republicanism.

state-harmful.rationale: Kirk rejects anarchy as well as tyranny, so the state is held necessary though limited.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from localism and distrust of federal power; the sources do not address guns directly.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from law-and-order rhetoric, though the movement opposes foreign military adventures.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the enduring moral order and traditional views of sexuality.

decide-locally.rationale: Localism, decentralisation and states' rights are core paleoconservative positions.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on moral order and responsibility.

traditional-family.rationale: Buchanan's speech defends family values as the core of the culture war.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Buchanan called equal legal standing for gay couples an amoral idea; paleoconservatives oppose gay marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Buchanan opposed abortion on demand and cited millions of unborn children destroyed.

more-religion-public.rationale: Supports voluntary school prayer and religious schooling and opposes church-state separation.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Paleoconservatives seek a rollback of multicultural programs and opposed desegregation.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the call to return to traditional ideals on gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: American nationalism and national identity are central themes.

gradual-change.rationale: Kirk stresses custom, continuity, prudence and balancing permanence with progression.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration restriction is a defining position; Buchanan proposed an annual cap near 250,000.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Buchanan wants soldiers to defend the US not the UN and rejects a New World Order.

free-trade.rationale: Paleoconservatives back tariffs and economic nationalism and oppose free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Buchanan argues what is good for global business is not necessarily good for America.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Favours non-intervention and rejects Pax Americana; force only for vital interests.

open-borders.rationale: Opposes large-scale demographic change and favours immigration restriction.

limit-growth.rationale: Buchanan attacked environmental extremists for putting nature ahead of workers and jobs.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from hostility to environmental regulation that costs workers' jobs.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Kirk's principle of imperfectability rejects utopian faith in progress.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kirk's prudence and continuity principles counsel against upheaval.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from hostility to centralised bureaucracy and distant elites.

central-planning.rationale: Rejects involuntary collectivism and central direction.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from the property principle and rejection of collectivism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the property principle and emphasis on generational continuity.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from criticism of welfare and its effects on communities.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariffs and protectionism are core to the movement's economic nationalism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic nationalism suggests some support, but the Old Right strand opposes state direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's property principle and local, voluntary community.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Contradicts the defence of property and freedom.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from rejection of centralised direction.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kirk's restraints on power and paleoconservative republicanism oppose it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Burkean sympathies exist but monarchy is not a stated program.

democracy-best.rationale: Paleoconservatives champion republicanism and are wary of democracy as such.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from republicanism and limits on popular passion.

workers-councils.rationale: Contrary to inherited institutions and private property.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from states' rights and Southern traditionalist strands.

natural-rulers.rationale: Kirk valued orders and classes reflecting natural distinctions.

political-violence-never.rationale: Prudence counsels against it but no categorical position is stated.

war-builds-character.rationale: Anti-imperialist adherents reject war for its own sake.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Kirk grounds law in a transcendent order and Christian ethics, short of scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's rejection of anarchy.

military-superiority.rationale: Wants a strong defence but rejects Pax Americana and global commitments.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement stresses national identity and has increasingly focused on race.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Kirk's order and variety reject class conflict as the engine of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Kirk warns that forced uniformity weakens civilisation.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from opposition to multicultural programs.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from opposition to multicultural and race-conscious programs.

civilizational-union.rationale: National independence is preferred over supranational unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Kirk's moral order stresses duty and responsibility over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from voluntary community and enduring moral order.

limit-population.rationale: Pro-family stance conflicts with limits, while immigration restriction pulls the other way.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's valuing of existing civilisation and its institutions.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Kirk's prudence and continuity oppose speeding disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the enduring moral order and prudence.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from prudence and distrust of centralisation.

restore-past-order.rationale: Claims authentic tradition against neoconservatism, though Kirk balances permanence with progression.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Kirk's prudence principle judges policy by probable long-run consequences.

direct-action.rationale: Prudence and respect for institutions favour ordinary politics.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Contradicts Kirk's variety and property principles.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from the defence of property and markets.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contrary to restraints on power and property.

collective-farming.rationale: Contrary to property and voluntary community.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Buchanan blames empire and entangling commitments, not capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Property is valued, but the state is held necessary.

harm-principle.rationale: Moral order is a legitimate basis for law.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Voluntary community and tradition are given weight over individualism.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from the view that the state serves moral and communal ends.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the property and limited-state emphasis.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to cultural elites and federal think tanks.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Some figures have asserted racial differences but there is no consensus.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's voluntary community and orders of society.

total-state.rationale: Kirk opposes involuntary collectivism and concentrated power.

national-rebirth.rationale: Buchanan's culture war framing speaks of a fight for the soul of America.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Paleoconservatives are anti-imperialist; A Republic, Not an Empire.

universal-morality.rationale: Kirk affirms an enduring moral order grounded in natural law or revelation.

single-common-good.rationale: Kirk's variety principle values diverse interests and institutions.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Adherents are split, with Buchanan critical and Gottfried pro-Israel.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Contrary to property and Kirk's rejection of collectivism.

school-vouchers.rationale: Buchanan backed freedom to choose religious schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from Old Right fiscal conservatism.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic nationalists and market conservatives differ.

national-self-determination.rationale: Buchanan stresses national independence and a republic not an empire.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposes UN authority, though force is only for vital interests.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kirk grounds order in tradition, prescription and transcendent order.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from immigration restriction and criticism of welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from criticism of welfare and dependency.

class-collaboration.rationale: Kirk values orders and classes in harmony rather than conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Kirk prizes custom, continuity and inherited institutions.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Return to traditional gender ideals; Buchanan opposed women in combat units.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred from the property and commerce emphasis.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement opposed desegregation in its Southern strand, but mainstream adherents do not press for race-classifying law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Adherents blame a managerial class, not the state as such.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from criticism of environmental regulation hurting jobs.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Rollback of multicultural programs and emphasis on national culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Opposition to demographic change exists but no consensus on conspiracy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from preference for existing republican institutions.

national-mission.rationale: Buchanan rejects Pax Americana and a mission abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Traditionalist views on gender oppose the premise.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from moral order and respect for human life.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Limited but not minimal state; moral order is public concern.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred; the sources record no explicit endorsement by mainstream adherents.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kirk's enduring moral order is compatible, though he defends natural distinctions.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from American nationalism and pride in national origins.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from preference for voluntary community.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an issue in the tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Buchanan supports voluntary school prayer and religious schooling.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred from republicanism and voluntary community.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism favours protecting domestic producers.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred; sources record no mainstream endorsement.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian overlap but adherents are split.

separated-powers.rationale: Kirk's ninth principle calls for checks, balances and restraints on power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Contrary to restraints on power and gradual change.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from criticism of welfare programs.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Restricting immigration and rolling back multiculturalism rest on this premise.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to republicanism and natural distinctions.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on restraints on power.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the property and free-market emphasis.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contrary to freedom and restraints on power.

party-commands-army.rationale: Contrary to restraints on power and separation of powers.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from the republican view of representation.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Buchanan opposes supranational bodies and world government.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Buchanan criticises war without congressional approval.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Adherents are Protestant and Catholic and split.

clerical-rule.rationale: Contrary to republicanism and restraints on power.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Concern with moral order exists but no stated censorship program.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Paleoconservatives attack out-of-touch federal elites, think tanks and neoconservative insiders.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's preference for prudence and individual judgement within institutions.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Buchanan would wind down NATO and end Asian security treaties so allies defend themselves.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Kirk's principles tie liberty to private property, so a ban on renting would be rejected; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Paleoconservatives defend gun rights and a non-interventionist force, but still treat a professional national army as normal; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Localism and attachment to community and tradition lead to a preference for small-town and rural life over the metropolis; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; Buchanan's non-interventionism cuts against foreign border projects while nationalism favours national unity.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Paleoconservatives attack a managerial and academic elite as detached from ordinary Americans; inferred from that critique.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Paleoconservatives oppose multiculturalism and defend Western and Christian civilisation as the basis of American identity.

death-penalty.rationale: Law-and-order conservatives of this camp, Buchanan included, generally support capital punishment; not a defining issue.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Buchanan's culture-war speech defends the traditional family against the cultural left and its agenda in schools.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious conservatives among them favour it, but many followers of Kirk accept evolution and treat it as a local matter; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The culture-war platform stresses moral order and public decency, which supports legal limits on pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Paleoconservatives hold national identity to rest on a people and culture and favour restricting immigration; inferred that birthright citizenship would be curtailed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Insistence on one common national culture and language, and opposition to multiculturalism, implies opposing state support for minority languages; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Defence of Christian ethics and religious liberty against secular regulation implies sympathy for exemptions; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Kirk's principles prize custom, convention and prescription over individual innovation; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's prudence and respect for contracts and from Buchanan's hostility to foreign aid and bailouts; not a defining issue.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the movement prizes national independence for its own sake and favours economic nationalism, not transforming the property system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Kirk's principles favour prescriptive, gradual change through inherited institutions over remaking the constitution from scratch.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's call for ordered liberty and restraints on power; paleoconservatives do not trade liberty for developmental growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Buchanan argues for ending foreign aid and putting American interests and citizens first.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: Buchanan wants allies to defend themselves while America remains a sovereign republic able to defend itself.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's Burkean preference for the Constitution's original design and mediated institutions; not stated.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred: some strands distrust the Federal Reserve while others want sound money kept from political direction, so adherents split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national identity and the nation as a rooted historic community.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Kirk ties property to moral order and duty, though paleoconservatives also defend private ownership against the state; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Inferred: American anticommunists of this tradition saw the USSR as a socialist or communist tyranny rather than capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of the managerial regulatory state; Kirk's prudence principle favours cautious change rather than pre-emptive restriction.

collective-defense.rationale: Buchanan opposes entangling alliances and open-ended commitments such as NATO's, arguing America should avoid being dragged into others' wars.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from its non-interventionism; paleoconservatives generally accept established borders and avoid crusades over annexations.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The movement stresses Christian ethics and a transcendent moral order, so it opposes curbing churches' independence or property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents accept a partisan US presidency but admire unifying national symbols.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from localism and the decentralist, secession-sympathetic strand of the movement; contested among adherents.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Localism and voluntary community, as in Kirk's principles, favour regions keeping their own laws and institutions.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred from Christian republican traditions in the US, which reject divine descent for rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Adherents are split between populist economic nationalism and low-tax conservatives, and the sources do not address a flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's emphasis on innate human imperfection and permanent things over social engineering of character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's principles of constitutional restraint and a rule of law that binds rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist scepticism of utopian technological projects and a priority on home and nation.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from admiration for the balanced Anglo-American constitutional order and Burkean prescription.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from its republican and Christian traditions, which reject leader worship.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; traditional-family emphasis points both ways on custody presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist class-struggle framing is foreign to a tradition that stresses moral order and organic community; inferred from that.

land-redistribution.rationale: Kirk's principles tie property to freedom, so taking estates for redistribution is opposed.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between restraint abroad and sympathy with expelled populations, so inferred as neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The non-interventionist 'Republic, Not an Empire' stance opposes foreign adventures to claim territory; inferred from it.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Christian ethics are central, but the American tradition of religious liberty makes legal punishment unlikely; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Cultural traditionalists favour modesty but not legal mandates in a Western constitutional order; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Paleoconservatives defend national sovereignty and oppose supranational bodies such as the euro-style arrangements.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Localism and national identity favour the nation-state over cross-border unions; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Opposition to multiculturalism means minorities are expected to assimilate to the common national culture.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between assimilationist emphasis and general liberty, so inferred as neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Kirk's first principle holds that a transcendent moral order, not material forces, governs society.

ban-cartels.rationale: Populist distrust of big business is offset by a tradition-minded wariness of state economic power; adherents are split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Opposition to the managerial state and to bailouts in the populist right suggests rejecting them; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Wary of judicial activism but equally of unchecked majorities (Kirk's prudence and ordered liberty); split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Buchanan's culture-war speech attacks radical feminism and the equality agenda; quotas by sex fit that opposition.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Protectionism is a documented plank, but a closed bloc with colonies is beyond it, so mildly opposed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Prefers tariffs and sovereignty over trade agreements and their binding standards; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Stresses moral duty but through family, church and community, not state-run incentive schemes; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Kirk's principle of prudence and distrust of abstract revolutionary schemes rejects engineered revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Kirk upholds orders and classes and prescriptive social differences rather than levelling.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The culture-war platform defends teaching the nation's own heritage and moral tradition in schools.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Buchanan's 'Republic, not an Empire' rejects ruling other peoples, even in the name of improving them.

patriotic-education.rationale: Stress on national identity and traditional moral education implies schools should foster patriotic loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from paleoconservative opposition to the managerial state and identity-based programmes; no specific source opened.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: paleoconservatives lean to sound money and distrust centralised institutions, so a state money monopoly is unlikely.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's emphasis on prudence, property and ordered continuity over theories of inevitable collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Buchanan argues the republic should not pursue empire or entangling influence abroad.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from economic nationalism and protectionism applied consistently to all nations.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: paleoconservatives reject class analysis and blame free trade for harming domestic workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the property-rights emphasis and the paleoconservative critique of anti-discrimination law as managerial overreach.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Kirk's principles stress restraints on power and constitutional order, which an entrenched bill of rights embodies.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from its respect for inherited treaties and legal continuity, though it supports national sovereignty claims.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from its Burkean respect for inherited institutions and prescriptive order over abstract election principles.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from its stress on community and tradition, though unanimity is not a conservative principle.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from its Burkean attachment to constitutional order and the rule of law.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from its preference for representative, constitutional government and legislative sovereignty over executive power.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Adherents are split between traditionalist views and compassion for animals; not a defining issue.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalism and agrarian roots, which accept humane animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Kirk's principles stress that the privileged have duties to the community, a traditional paternalist view.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from its stress on civic duty and community, though it is hostile to the modern state.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Adherents criticise mass culture and media as corrosive, but the claim is a leftist one that it doesn't take a side on.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Adherents criticise cultural elites shaping norms, but it isn't defined on this question.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist and anti-globalist stance, with sympathy for the claim but not for the exploitation framing.

native-born-offices.rationale: Its nationalism and focus on national identity favour reserving public office for native-born citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed; the statement's communist or socialist framing doesn't fit.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Opposes foreign aid and entangling alliances and supports self-reliance, as in Buchanan's non-interventionism.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Adherents are split; non-interventionism opposes wars to reclaim territory, but national claims may be sympathetic.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Rejects racial-group precedence and identity-based political leadership as contrary to its national identity and equal-citizenship principle.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to the antifascist left and its focus on national tradition over anti-fascism as a constitutional value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from its anti-communism and opposition to modern totalitarianism of any kind.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Adherents are split; some Southern traditionalists contest the dominant account.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Defends inherited tradition and heritage, including Confederate and historical monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from its critique of feminism and focus on traditional family issues, including concern for men.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from its critique of feminism, though not a defining issue.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rejects universalist exporting of democracy; Buchanan opposes remaking other nations in the American image.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Stresses civilian control of the military, though it values martial virtues.

paid-care-work.rationale: Defends the traditional family; paid domestic work is seen as a leftist idea.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on family, moral order and inherited duties.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from preference for locally rooted, traditional leaders over technocratic selection.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Favours protectionism and national economic control.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from defence of the traditional family as stated in the culture war speech.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from the Burkean view that representatives exercise prudent judgment.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from defence of existing entitlements and distrust of financial-market reforms.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Holds property and freedom to be inseparably connected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from its call for prudent restraints on power and constitutional government.

single-official-language.rationale: Stresses national identity and opposes multiculturalism.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its immigration restriction and national identity focus.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Opposes multiculturalism and the managerial state's equality enforcement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from its critique of materialism in favour of moral order.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Argues for a republic, not an empire, and against imperial interference.

corporate-influence.rationale: Paleoconservatives attack multinational and managerial-elite power, so they would likely agree; inferred, not a defining issue.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national sovereignty and distrust of the UN and global institutions.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from pro-family politics and immigration restriction, which leave births as the way to sustain the nation.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: localism favours community control, but Kirk's defence of private property makes limits on buyers uncomfortable.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from opposition to federal programmes and the managerial state.

democratic-peace.rationale: Buchanan rejects democracy crusades and nation-building abroad as imperial overreach.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Kirk's principles stress prescription, custom and law as the base of ordered liberty, so obedience is the default.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement opposes interventionism and empire, though 'for any reason' is stronger than most adherents state.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Old Right dislike of unions and the lack of any stated labour-organisation programme.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream adherents reject conspiracy theories about minorities, though critics allege some fringe tolerance; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The culture-war stance defends traditional marriage and family as the basis of society.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from distrust of the federal bureaucracy and the managerial state.

local-production.rationale: Economic nationalism, protectionism and localism favour producing and buying near home.

informal-organisation.rationale: Kirk values permanent institutions and associations over improvised groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Buchanan insists on US sovereignty against the UN, treaties and international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Buchanan frames America as a Christian-heritage nation, but the movement's identity is also cultural and civic; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Buchanan opposes subordination to foreign powers and wants a republic that deals with others as a sovereign equal, not through tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the localist, anti-centralist stress on regional and community self-government; not a stated programme.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: Kirk defends private property as tied to freedom, so common ownership of productive property is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-communist heritage and Cold War conservatism; the post-1991 focus is on non-intervention, so adherents are not eager for crusades.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: adherents distrust the managerial state but also market consolidation; no settled position on service delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Kirk grounds order in a transcendent moral order and Buchanan treats Christian faith as the base of the nation, so religion is no mere illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: paleoconservatives criticise global capitalism and corporate power yet defend property and markets, so they are split on its historical role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the defence of traditional family roles in the culture-war speech; adherents reject economic transformation as a route to equality.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the defence of the family and opposition to the managerial welfare state taking over family functions.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: adherents defend national language and culture but no official purge programme is stated.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from respect for constitutional order and inherited obligations; the issue is not addressed by the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from the localist defence of nation, family and private property against collectivism and utopian communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from restrictionist, anti-multicultural nationalism that favours consent and freedom; state-steered settlement conflicts with its limited-government localism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects both global capitalism and socialism in favour of tradition, localism and protectionism, but this is not a stated slogan.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed by the movement as such; adherents split on Israel and on land claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial is not part of the movement's doctrine; inferred, though some fringe figures have been accused of it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditional moral order supports disapproval, but localism and distrust of the state split adherents on criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Opposes the centralised managerial state and values ordered liberty and local self-government; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Christian moral order is central, but the movement prefers local custom to civil enforcement of doctrine; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Strongly anti-imperial: Buchanan's 'A Republic, Not an Empire' opposes overseas dominion.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that the movement sees it as a foreign religious doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from its constitutionalism and respect for national sovereignty; not addressed.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from localism and distrust of distant bureaucracy, though not from a source on participatory democracy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Opposes multiculturalism and identity-based politics, treating them as divisive.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Defends traditional moral order in the culture war, as in Buchanan's 1992 convention speech.

assisted-dying.rationale: Rooted in Christian ethics and the sanctity of life; Buchanan is strongly pro-life.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: paleoconservatives define themselves against the left and also against neoconservatives, rather than as beyond left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from its defence of property and market order; the Marxian alienation thesis is not discussed.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Immigration restriction and national-identity stress imply scepticism toward large-scale Muslim immigration; inferred, adherents differ.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Kirk's Ten Conservative Principles begins with belief in a transcendent moral order and divine intent ruling society.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from its stress on Christian tradition and public religious expression.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from scepticism toward regulation and federal mandates, though some adherents are indifferent.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: prefers local and traditional economies and protectionism over a managed social-market synthesis.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Favours national defence and sovereignty; it opposes foreign intervention, not armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; economic nationalists favour protectionism, but whether regions may grow rich first is not discussed.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Opposes entangling alliances and neoconservative interventionism; Buchanan argues for non-intervention and against NATO expansion.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: American paleoconservatives defend inherited institutions and the Republic's constitutional order, which has no hereditary office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from its defence of private property and distrust of schemes of state or collective finance; not a stated issue.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from its economic nationalism and hostility to international institutions that constrain national sovereignty.

property-franchise.rationale: Paleoconservatives value property and stability but work within universal suffrage; revival of a property franchise is not a stated aim.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Its traditionalism rejects ecofeminist critiques of gender hierarchy and the framing of the order of nature as domination.

reification.rationale: Inferred: it defends the market order and rejects Marxist analysis, though it criticises corporate globalism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: it rejects the Marxist claim that freedoms are hollow under private ownership, but distrusts mainstream media and elite cultural institutions.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Kirk's principles stress prescription, custom and constitutional restraint on power, favouring settled law over arbitrary rule.

racial-franchise.rationale: Critics accuse the movement of ethnic nationalism, but its adherents' stated positions are for a civic republic with universal citizenship; limiting the vote by race is not a stated aim.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from its preference for local, rooted, prudential self-government over mass direct participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of federal bureaucracy and demand for accountability; not stated in the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: It stresses Christian cultural tradition, but legal limits on interfaith marriage conflict with American constitutional liberties; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: it defends a Christian-inflected national culture but does not advocate economic targeting of a religious minority.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from Kirk-style preference for prescriptive institutions, representative government and distrust of novel democratic engineering; not discussed by the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's defence of a transcendent moral order and inherited tradition and Buchanan's traditional Christian stance; modernising doctrine is not directly addressed.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred: Buchanan-style populism distrusts global corporate and financial elites, and Kirk warned against concentrated power of all kinds.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Culture war speech opposes the movement for gay rights as an attack on traditional values; inferred opposition to open service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Kirk's principles ground order in religious tradition and the culture war speech defends religion against secular state power.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Order and the rule of law are conservative priorities and abolition contradicts prudence and tradition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its preference for a unified national culture and rejection of multicultural arrangements.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Kirk's principles stress voluntary community and local institutions over centralised state action.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: Buchanan campaigned against career politicians, though Kirk's prudence principle gives no explicit support.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the preference for a republic over direct popular rule and its defense of constitutional limits.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as indifferent, with a focus on national and cultural survival rather than global risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its defence of traditional religion and traditional gender roles.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its defence of the traditional family, with some adherents accepting shared authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Immigration restriction and national identity are defining themes, which implies reserving political rights to citizens.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's principle that property and freedom are linked, and from distrust of regulation.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Kirk's defence of property and settled order.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from localism and distrust of the central state.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from non-intervention, though a defensive deterrent is accepted.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Buchanan's case that the republic should not be an empire calls for bringing troops and bases home.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from scepticism toward moralised foreign and historical politics.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Kirk's defence of property as a pillar of order.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditional moral order, which allows self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the stress on tradition and a national identity inherited across generations.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Buchanan's culture war speech defends traditional views of sex and family against what he called radical change.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the culture war stance against feminism and gender theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's reverence for tradition and the dead, though martyr language is not typical.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Buchanan called the conflict a religious war for the soul of America.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no settled view.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's view that moral and cultural order underlie sound politics.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the defence of traditional Christian practice.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the defence of traditional Christian authority against feminist critique.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national identity and opposition to multiculturalism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from localism and a settled, historical map of regions.

independent-unions.rationale: Not a defining issue; the Old Right distrusts both organised labour and state control, so adherents plausibly split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from paleoconservative hostility to socialism: state ownership would be counted as socialism whoever rules, so the workers' power test is not their concern.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: localism favours local public services, but suspicion of government and of the managerial state pulls the other way.

second-chamber.rationale: Kirk's principles call for balanced and restrained power, and the American tradition of a Senate alongside the House fits that.

municipal-property.rationale: Kirk's principles treat private property as linked to freedom; communal ownership of the means of production is a socialist idea.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: localism favours local decision, but no source discusses assembly confederations and adherents also value national sovereignty.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the family-centred platform of Buchanan's culture-war speech and the protectionist aim of keeping wages up for working families.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents could favour less regulation or caution about medical ethics and the managerial state, so this is inferred as split.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's wariness of radical change and of schemes that treat human nature as improvable by public programmes.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: distrust of the managerial state favours financial privacy, but concern for order and law enforcement favours traceability.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: distrust of state and corporate surveillance favours anonymity, while concern for public order and moral standards cuts against it.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's principle of ordered liberty and restraints on power, though paleoconservatives weight community, tradition and nation heavily too.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Kirk's first principle is belief in a transcendent moral order, and the movement stresses Christian ethics and moral order.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from American localism and federalism, under which states' powers are entrenched rather than at Congress's discretion.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; agrarian and localist suspicion of agribusiness competes with market and progress arguments.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the movement's localism, small-town and rural attachments and hostility to managerial planning.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mixed: some paleoconservatives defend a European-American or Western identity, but most frame it as culture and nation, not racial political organising; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: the movement defends ancestry, heritage and national identity against multiculturalism, though many avoid racial framing.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Buchanan's A Republic, Not an Empire argues against foreign entanglements and for using force only for vital national interests.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The movement stresses shared heritage and culture as national identity but is split on defining it by language and on ethnic framing; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Its emphasis on a unified national culture and a common republic opposes sectarian electorates; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Suspicion of globalist and foreign interference is common, but claims of plots to partition the US are not a settled position; inferred as split.

free-public-college.rationale: Opposition to federal spending and the managerial state, with scepticism of academia, implies opposing free tuition; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Opposes new federal taxes and central regulatory schemes, though some localist conservationists differ; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Kirk's principle of prudence and stewardship of the inherited order extends to the natural inheritance; inferred from his conservative principles.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Paleoconservatives stress traditional sex roles but not giving women's distinct values more political weight; adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Buchanan opposes foreign entanglements and military adventures but defends strong national defence; inferred as split.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Buchanan's anti-empire stance disliked secret commitments and entangling alliances made without public consent; inferred, low confidence.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic nationalists favour limiting capital flight and offshoring while market-minded members oppose controls; split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from its support for an armed citizenry and local self-reliance, over centralised state monopolies.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: It opposes foreign wars of intervention but values duty, order and loyalty, so would not urge refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from its preference for local, voluntary arrangements over centralised union bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: It dislikes the managerial state and redistributive tools; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's emphasis on prudence and limiting government.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: It advocates economic nationalism and protection and distrusts global institutions.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Kirk's principles stress continuity and prudent change, though it attacks the managerial state; it would reform rather than smash.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Its localism favours communities arranging their own affairs; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalist distrust of treating nature through economic abstraction.

sacred-nation.rationale: Buchanan and Kirk stress national identity and a transcendent moral order, though the nation is rarely called sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on personal responsibility and opposition to federal spending.

internal-colonialism.rationale: It rejects the framing of a nation's regions as colonies; inferred from its stress on national unity.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Kirk grounds order in a transcendent moral order and human nature, fixed rather than redesigned.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from its scepticism of state funding and of the cultural establishment attacked by Buchanan.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Paleoconservatives defend Christianity as the nation's moral basis, which implies it is distinct rather than one of many equal expressions; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Economic nationalists favour protecting domestic producers but also distrust state intervention; adherents are split and the sources do not say.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist defence of sovereignty; it opposes foreign entanglements but not national deterrence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Buchanan sought to win working-class voters inside the Republican Party, not through a separate class party; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from its moral-order conservatism and opposition to practices alien to Western culture; not addressed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Property rights are central to its principles and are held as a legal right for citizens generally; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by paleoconservatism; no basis for a stance.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Kirk-style prudence and stewardship accept law that restrains harm to others, without insisting on courts only; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: An American constitutional movement with no tradition of chiefs in lawmaking; inferred rejection.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Stresses property and limits on power over centralised regulation, though it values conservation; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Law-and-order stance in the Buchanan speech supports firm punishment; mandatory terms are inferred from that.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Wants lower immigration and assimilation to a common American culture, which includes English as the national language.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the localist, anti-managerial-state stance and the American right's right-to-work tradition; not a defining issue.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national identity and citizenship and opposition to mass immigration; the sources do not discuss ballot rules.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the stress on a Christian moral order and inherited tradition, which sits badly with legal parity among interpretations; not directly addressed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Paleoconservatives prize tradition, moral order and a republic of limited, rooted government over mere procedure, so elections alone do not make a government legitimate.

premarital-sex.rationale: Kirk's principles and the Buchanan speech defend traditional moral order and Christian ethics, which treat sex outside marriage as wrong.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the suspicion of centralised state power and the order-and-authority emphasis; the question is anachronistic and adherents may split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from opposition to the managerial welfare state, though a cash scheme is a market-style idea and many would still prefer family and community aid.

women-suffrage.rationale: Paleoconservatives accept the established franchise, though some such as Gottfried-circle writers criticise its effects; the majority view accepts equal political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Paleoconservatives defend Christian ethics and the traditional family as sources of order and reject the feminist claim that religion oppresses women.

race-social-construct.rationale: Paleoconservatives stress inherited national and cultural identity and many treat race as a real category, so they would resist calling it merely constructed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Paleoconservatives oppose the managerial state and feminist state projects, favouring the traditional family over dedicated gender-equality bureaucracies.

missingStatements.text: My country should end its permanent military alliances and bring its troops home from abroad.
missingStatements.rationale: Buchanan would wind down NATO and end Asian security treaties so allies defend themselves.

notes: Strands differ: Southern traditionalists, Old Right fiscal conservatives, economic nationalists and race-focused writers answer some economic and race items differently.
